title: How to Freeze Your Credit for Free
bigPicture: A credit freeze stops anyone from opening a new credit account in your name, it does not affect your credit score, and it is free to place and to lift.
whatYouNeedToKnow: There is no cost to place or lift a credit freeze.
You must contact all three credit bureaus: Equifax, Experian, and TransUnion.
While a freeze is on, nobody can open a new credit account in your name.
A freeze does not affect your credit score.
A freeze lasts until you lift it.
commonMistakesToAvoid: Freezing at only one bureau. Contact all three.
Forgetting how to lift the freeze before you apply for credit. Keep the details each bureau gives you somewhere safe.
Leaving it frozen when you need a loan. Lift it first so the lender can check your credit.
actionSteps: Gather the details the bureaus ask for, such as your name, address, birth date, and Social Security number.
Contact Equifax, Experian, and TransUnion and ask each one to place a freeze.
Write down and safely store whatever each bureau gives you to lift the freeze later.
When a lender needs to check your credit, ask which bureau they will use, lift the freeze there, and put it back afterward.
